newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles higher on cash, natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles higher on cash, natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Thursday, taking a cue from stronger natural gas futures and steady cash market prices in the western U.S.
"It was following cash, following natural gas," said a Houston futures trader.

June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up 36 cents at $14.35 a megawatt hour (MWh), near the day's high at $14.40. July COB finished up 16 cents at $16.30. Other COB months ended five to 20 cents higher.
June Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 45 cents at $19.60 after traded between $19.20 and $19.65. July PV finished up 41 cents at $23.76. Deferred PV contracts ended down 15 to up 34 cents.
Spot physical prices in the Northwest were supported by cooler-than-normal spring weather, while those in the Southwest by hotter-than-normal temperatures, traders said.
Day-ahead electricity prices for firm, peak delivery at COB were little changed at $16.50-17.50, while those at PV narrowed to $19.25-20.00 from $19.00-21.00 yesterday.
NYMEX June Henry Hub natgas futures settled up 59 cents at $2.243 per million British thermal units after hitting a session high at $2.280.
Spot electricity supply across the West remained tight.

Hydropower availability in Northwest has been reduced due to flood control measures in effect in British Columbia and Bonneville Power Administration still limiting daily offers for peak demand hours.
About 4,000 MW of generating capacity in the Southwest is said to be currently offline for repairs or maintenance, but much of the capacity is expected to return to service later this month.
Brokers and traders expect the complex to continue this week's rise as short-term outlook for physical power and gas prices remained bulllish.

In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be about five degrees Fahrenheit below normal in the northeast to about six degrees above normal in the southeast over the next several days, with generally dry conditions expected.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average near normal over the next several days, with generally unsettled weather and some patches of precipitation.
